card: Makes addrman address selection inside buckets uniformly random across occupied slots. Previously, selecting from a bucket used a linear scan from a random start offset, which heavily biased peer selection toward addresses following large runs of empty slots (up to 95.3% versus 4.7% in a two-address bucket). The PR copies occupied bucket entries into a temporary buffer, samples uniformly while respecting network filtering, and adds chi-square uniformity unit tests and fuzz checks.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the selection logic; minor diff updates likely from a rebase.
evidence: PR description: 'This means that if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).'
PR description notes the bias was 'Suggested by Crypt-iQ. Also pointed out earlier by mzumsande in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23140#discussion_r733084509.'
problem: Selecting an address from an addrman bucket currently scans sequentially from a randomly chosen slot in the 64-slot bucket until an entry is found. In buckets with few entries, this severely biases selection toward whichever address follows a long run of empty slots (for instance, 95.3% versus 4.7% in a two-entry bucket), skewing peer connection selection.

risk.why: A flaw in the bucket sampling loop could lead to infinite loops or biased peer selection, degrading node connectivity and eclipse resistance.

summary: Switches address sampling within addrman buckets to uniform random selection across occupied slots. Instead of choosing a random offset and linearly scanning until finding an occupied entry, non-empty entries are gathered into a temporary buffer and chosen with equal probability while filtering by network. A chi-square unit test and a fuzz assertion verify the uniform distribution and network filtering.
